title: A determinant-trivial chain automorphism lifting a local homotopy
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring (a commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal), and let $P=[P^{-1}\xrightarrow{d_P}P^0]$, $Q=[Q^{-1}\xrightarrow{d_Q}Q^0]$ be complexes of finite free $R$-modules, zero in other degrees [def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $a,b:P\to Q$ be morphisms surjective in both degrees, and let $h:P^0\to Q^{-1}$ be $R$-linear with $b^0-a^0=d_Qh$ and $b^{-1}-a^{-1}=hd_P$. There is a submodule $U\subseteq P^{-1}$ such that both $a^{-1}|_U$ and $b^{-1}|_U$ are isomorphisms onto $Q^{-1}$. Let $s:Q^{-1}\to P^{-1}$ be the inverse of $a^{-1}|_U$ followed by the inclusion, and put $t=sh$. Then $a^{-1}t=h$, $k^{-1}=1+td_P$ and $k^0=1+d_Pt$ define a chain automorphism $k:P\xrightarrow{\sim}P$ with $ak=b$. More precisely in $P^{-1}=\ker a^{-1}\oplus U$, $k^{-1}$ has block form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\ C&B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ with $B=(a^{-1}|_U)^{-1}(b^{-1}|_U)$, so its inverse has blocks $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\-B^{-1}C&B^{-1}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; if $w=(k^{-1})^{-1}$, then $(k^0)^{-1}=1-d_Pwt$. In any finite bases $\det(k^0)=\det(k^{-1})$. Thus the induced automorphism $D(k)=\det(k^0)\otimes(\det(k^{-1})^{-1})^\vee$ of $D(P)=\det_R(P^0)\otimes_R\det_R(P^{-1})^\vee$ is the identity, where $\det_R$ is the top exterior power [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] and $\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,R)$.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), first two and final paragraphs, and Tag 0FJF (lemma-det-switch); explicit inverse refinement of the block calculation.

proof.text: Choose finite bases of $P^{-1}$ and $Q^{-1}$, giving isomorphisms $P^{-1}\simeq R^{\oplus n}$ and $Q^{-1}\simeq R^{\oplus m}$ by [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Apply [lem-trf-local-common-summand-surjections] to the coordinate versions of $a^{-1},b^{-1}$; the ring is local and both maps are surjective by hypothesis. Transport its submodule back to $P^{-1}$. It gives the required $U$, both restriction isomorphisms, and $P^{-1}=\ker(a^{-1})\oplus U$. Define $s$ as in the statement, so $a^{-1}s=1$ and $\operatorname{im}(s)\subseteq U$.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), first two and final proof paragraphs; explicit algebraic refinement.

proof.text: Set $t=sh$, $K=1+td_P$ on $P^{-1}$ and $L=1+d_Pt$ on $P^0$. Then $a^{-1}t=h$. Direct expansion gives $d_PK=Ld_P$, so $(K,L)$ is a chain endomorphism. Also $a^{-1}K=a^{-1}+hd_P=b^{-1}$, while $a^0L=a^0+a^0d_Pt=a^0+d_Qa^{-1}t=a^0+d_Qh=b^0$, using the chain-map identity for $a$ and the two given homotopy equations. Thus $ak=b$ degreewise.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), first two and final proof paragraphs; explicit algebraic refinement.

proof.text: Write $N=\ker(a^{-1})$. Since $td_P$ has image in $U$, the $N$-component of $K$ on $N\oplus U$ is the projection to $N$. On $U$, its $U$-component is $B=(a^{-1}|_U)^{-1}(b^{-1}|_U)$: both maps take values in $U$ and applying the injective $a^{-1}|_U$ gives $b^{-1}|_U$. On $N$ put $C=td_P|_N:N\to U$. Hence $K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\ C&B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, with $B$ invertible. Multiplying in both orders shows that $w=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\-B^{-1}C&B^{-1}\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ satisfies $wK=Kw=1$. No basis or freeness assertion for $N$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), first two and final proof paragraphs; explicit algebraic refinement.

proof.text: Put $V=1-d_Pwt$ on $P^0$. The identities $(1+td_P)w=w(1+td_P)=1$ give $wt+td_Pwt=t$ and $wt+wtd_Pt=t$, respectively, after right composition with $t$. Therefore $LV=1+d_P(t-wt-td_Pwt)=1$ and $VL=1+d_P(t-wt-wtd_Pt)=1$. Thus $L^{-1}=V$. Multiplying $d_PK=Ld_P$ on the left by $V$ and on the right by $w$ gives $Vd_P=d_Pw$, so the degreewise inverses form a chain map. This proves the chain-automorphism assertion with the stated inverse formula, without any quasi-isomorphism hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0FJK (lemma-homotopic-surjections), first two and final proof paragraphs; explicit algebraic refinement.

proof.text: In any chosen finite bases let $D$ represent $d_P$ and $T$ represent $t$. The matrices of $L$ and $K$ are $I+DT$ and $I+TD$, respectively. Apply [lem-trf-rectangular-determinant-switch] with $A=D$, $B=T$. Their rectangular sizes are the two finite ranks of $P$, so its hypotheses hold and it yields $\det(L)=\det(K)$ in these bases. In particular this includes either rank being zero.

source.place: Tag 0FJF (lemma-det-switch), rectangular-matrix identity; Tag 0FJK first proof paragraph.

proof.text: For a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of a finite free module, [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis] with $n=r$ shows that the top exterior power is free with basis the single element $e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r$ (for $r=0$ the generator is $1$). For an endomorphism with matrix $M$, multilinearity and alternation in [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] expand $Me_1\wedge\cdots\wedge Me_r$ in basis coordinates; terms with a repeated index vanish and reordering gives the sign, so the image is $\sum_{\sigma}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_i M_{\sigma(i),i}\,e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r=\det(M)\,e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r$. Thus the top exterior actions of $L$ and $K$ are multiplication by the same scalar $\delta$ of Step 5. The top exterior action is multiplicative on pure wedges, so the action of $w=K^{-1}$ is the inverse, $\delta$ is a unit and this action is multiplication by $\delta^{-1}$. Precomposition by that scalar on the dual line is again multiplication by $\delta^{-1}$. Consequently $D(k)$ multiplies the tensor of the top-wedge generator for $P^0$ and the dual generator for $P^{-1}$ by $\delta\delta^{-1}=1$. This tensor generates $D(P)$, hence $D(k)=1$.
